To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Fernhollow Photo is a real business now

[DRAFT — saving this to read over first. Please don't publish it yet, I want to go through it one more time and get Sam's blessing on the cake paragraph.]

Big news: Fernhollow Photo is a real business now, and it's mine!!

I know, I know. I wasn't going to announce anything until I had more weddings on the books, and then I filed the LLC on my lunch break, sitting in my car in a Fred Meyer parking lot, and cried a little in the drive-thru line, so clearly the secret phase is over.

Here's the whole thing, start to finish.

The name first, because it's the part I care about most.

Fernhollow is a trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. The fern hollow trail. That's where I took my first real pictures, on Grandma's Pentax, walking that path by myself and figuring out that I wanted to do this forever. Grandma, the name is yours. I'm naming a whole company after the place where you let me run around with that camera and shoot whatever I wanted. I never told you what that camera taught me. I'm telling you now.

How this happened.

Marisol called me on October 6 and told me Rosebud Lane was closing at the end of October. I shot for her for four years, and she is the reason I know basically everything I know about this job — how to work a room, how to make a nervous bride's mom laugh, what to do when the light does something weird right before the ceremony. Marisol, I have a whole shoutout for you and I want it on the record: you taught me everything, and half of what I've built is standing on your shoulders. Six of my 2027 couples found me because she sent them my way, and I'll be grateful about that for the rest of my career.

The numbers, because I promised myself I'd be honest.

14 weddings booked for 2027. Six came from Marisol's referrals, eight found me on my own, most of them from a set of couple photos I shot at Multnomah Falls for Marisol. The very first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken — June 12 at Timberline. They found me from those Falls pictures and emailed me to book, and then I had to sit in my car and be normal about it. June is my busiest month (four weddings!). The furthest one out is Wallowa Lake in September, which means I'm already past the part where this is brand new and slightly terrifying and into the part where it's just my job. Deposits are in. Website went live November 1. LLC filed October 22.

The scary part, and then the plan.

It's scary. I'm not going to pretend it isn't. Going out alone means every slow month is mine and every deposit is mine and there's nobody to text at 2am before a sunrise wedding. I have been quietly planning this in my head for two years, though, so it's a lot less spontaneous than the Fred Meyer parking lot makes it look.

And Dad: I got the health insurance. Marketplace plan, starts January 1. I know that's the thing you wanted to talk to me about, so let's just get it out here where nobody can corner me about it over the turkey. I'm covered, it's handled, it's done. (I'm not doing school portraits, just so we all know where I stand on that one.)

The rest of the plan is people. Jae second shoots the big weddings with me — the ones with two hundred guests and a venue that definitely does not have enough room — and he's paid per wedding, so that's a real arrangement and not a favor I'm quietly asking for. Sam is in my corner. Sam also made a cake that said FERNHOLOW, and we ate it anyway, because it tasted good and because arguing about spelling on a cake felt like a bad omen for the whole year.

So: LLC, website, health insurance, a second shooter, a full calendar, and a plan for the slow months. That's what "not reckless" looks like for me. Two years of thinking and about six months of paperwork.

One more thing.

I'm bringing the camera to Thanksgiving. If anybody wants family pictures, come find me — free, no package, no upsell, no "we'll throw in the dog." I'll put you in the good light at Ruthie's and I will absolutely put it on this blog, which is what I apparently do now, apparently with my whole chest.

I love you all. Come find me at Ruthie's, be nice to Sam, and Dad, we can talk about the insurance thing in the driveway where I can't escape.

See you all on Thanksgiving.

---

To: marisol@rosebudlanestudio.example
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow — you're in it

Hey Marisol,

I wanted you to hear this from me before it goes up, and I wanted to say it straight: I'm putting you in my announcement. Not any of the details — just that Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October, that you sent me six of my 2027 couples, and that you taught me basically everything I know. The rest of your story isn't mine to tell, so I left it out entirely.

It's saved as a draft on the family blog and I haven't published it. If you'd rather I take your name out, or take out the referral part, say the word and it's gone. No hard feelings either way, and honestly I'd completely understand.

For what it's worth: the website's live, I've got 14 weddings booked for 2027, and I got my health insurance sorted starting January 1. I'm okay. I'm really okay.

Six couples came to me because you sent them. That's the part I can't write down without crying in my car again.

Thank you. For real. For all of it, and for calling me first.

Tessa
